---
title: "Factorization"
---

Linguistic datasets often contain several measurements of the same objects. A vowel token may have values for several formants. A verb may have counts for several syntactic frames. A language may have a binary value for every segment represented in an inventory database.

These matrices can be large even when their columns share substantial structure. If several acoustic measurements rise together, or if sets of segments tend to recur across inventories, treating every cell as unrelated may obscure the common pattern.

Matrix factorization represents recurring patterns with fewer dimensions by rewriting a data matrix as products or sums of smaller matrices. The [unit of analysis introduced at the start of the course](../foundations/linguistic-data.qmd) still determines what one row represents. The resulting factorization can describe observations, describe variables, and reconstruct cells, but its interpretation remains tied to the objects and measurements placed in the original matrix.

## Representation, reconstruction, and retained rank

We will ask three questions in order.

1. What do the rows, columns, origins, and units mean?
2. How can one or more rank one patterns reconstruct the matrix?
3. How many patterns should be retained for the declared reconstruction task?

The order prevents a common interpretive shortcut. A component cannot be understood before the row and column representation is fixed, and a retained dimension cannot be justified before reconstruction has been defined.

## Chapter sequence

We begin with [linguistic data matrices](data-matrices.qmd), which fix the row objects and measurement columns. [Centering and scaling](centering-and-scaling.qmd) then define the coordinate system used to measure variation.

[Rank one structure](rank-one-structure.qmd) introduces a single outer-product pattern. [Singular value decomposition](singular-value-decomposition.qmd) orders several such patterns, and [principal component analysis](principal-component-analysis.qmd) applies that decomposition to variation around column means.

The final pages turn the representation back toward interpretation and evaluation. [Scores and loadings](scores-and-loadings.qmd) distinguish row coordinates from column directions. [Reconstruction](reconstruction.qmd) maps retained components back to cells and measures the residuals. [Choosing components](choosing-components.qmd) selects the retained rank on validation outcomes before a separate final evaluation.

## What factorization can establish

A successful low-rank reconstruction suggests that the chosen matrix contains recurring numerical structure. It does not by itself show that a component is a psychological variable, a universal phonological dimension, or a causal process.

This limitation is productive. It tells us what additional checks are needed: inspect the variables that define each direction, relate row scores to known sampling and provenance labels, and evaluate reconstruction on cells that did not determine the representation.

By the end of the module, we should be able to reconstruct every matrix expression from its row and column meanings, reproduce each hand calculation in R, and state exactly what a retained component does and does not license us to claim.
